gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the parking-mode cable costs or what voltage it cuts off at: Vantrue's kit that names the S1 Pro is $29.99 and cuts power at 11.6, 12.0 or 12.4 V, so the $79.99 S1 Pro with parking recording comes to $109.98, over the $100 line.
standout_why: Compared against carcody.com and rottenwifi.com (both cited) and dealdey.com (rank 1), all opened 2026-11-21. Carcody and rottenwifi already state the mechanism itself: the accessory socket often loses power with the ignition, a supercapacitor only closes the last file, and parking recording needs a hardwire kit with low-voltage cutoff. Dealdey says a hardwire kit, OBD adapter or always-on outlet is needed. None gives a kit price, a cutoff voltage, or the camera-plus-kit total against $100, and none covers the Vantrue S1 Pro, Vantrue Element 1 Lite or DDPAI Mini Pro 4K. Carcody and rottenwifi list the VIOFO A119 Mini 2 as '2K at up to 60fps' with HDR but do not say HDR drops it to 30 fps. dashanddrive.com (cited in the second chat) could not be opened (certificate error), so it is not compared.
decides: For a shopper who only wants driving footage, the Vantrue S1 Pro 1-channel at $79.99 stays inside $100 and the mechanism changes nothing. For a shopper who wants parking recording inside $100, the S1 Pro goes over once Vantrue's kit is added ($104.98 with the $24.99 universal kit, $109.98 with the $29.99 kit that names the S1 Pro). Two partner-store options stay under: the DDPAI Mini Pro 4K sold with its hardwire kit at $69.00, and the Vantrue Element 1 Lite (1-channel, 1080p 30 fps) at $69.99 plus a $24.99 or $29.99 kit ($94.98 or $99.98). ChatGPT's first-run top pick, the VIOFO A119 Mini 2, is $159.99 on VIOFO's US store today, so it is out on budget before the kit ($17.99) is counted.
